records.scope: The final three Rebels guides, four numbered parts: selected episode connections, eight introductory supporting identities and four additive facts. All 53 narrative and sixteen trivia captions read, with individually cited released stills. Existing identities, episode register, dates, credits and earlier evidence retained.
limitations: All 66 registered Rebels guides /75 numbered parts now have a scoped selected-profile review. This batch checks the final three guides against 293 selected records, not a complete frame, voice, credit or every-character inventory. Other previously open scene identifications remain open.

World Between Worlds distinguishes physical realm visitors, past portal scenes, named reused voices, magical remote Palpatine, Morai/Daughter and attributed Dume interpretation. Fool’s Hope separates captured AT-AT base, earlier AT-TE, planned betrayal, discarded Krennic and unnamed blockade ships.

The combined finale preserves parts 15–16 as one guide, main battle versus epilogue, holo Palpatine, stored/tempting parent images, Ezra farewell recording, actual purrgil, named Chimaera/transported Temple fragment, later Lira San and unknown destination. No Endor/Peridea scene or universal body/identity rule inferred.

Crawler Commandeers separates actual ore crawler, current named Guild personnel and physical Yavin briefing from elite readouts, a future factory target, World Devastator design ancestry and uncertain background identities. The current crawler/assault guide-number labels conflict with the retained register; no renumbering.

Rebel Assault establishes classic X-wing debut and actual elite fighter; Phoenix Two/Four, unnamed Lutrillian/script nickname and anonymous astromech/R3-A3 remain separate. The unused tower map is not an on-screen measured inventory. Cleat has only an introductory profile, without a selected episode-row identification.

Jedi Night retains its two inherited episode rows/evidence, adds individually cited rescue participants, gliders/animals and depot, and separately sources Kanan’s fate. Tarkin’s individual form remains unspecified. Generic walker/gunship words, Krennic mention and intended Coruscant travel do not certify extra type/person/world scenes.

Dume separates physical Rukh/Pryce, Thrawn’s hologram, reported death, wolf species and named giant of unknown nature. No Kanan spirit/identity merge, prior named-Dume appearance, Temple visit from a stone or physical factory from a shutdown report is inferred.

Wolves and a Door separates physical crew/Hydan, Emperor hologram, old Thrawn recording, unidentified voice montage, actual wolves and Mortis paintings. Hydan/Vaneé, animal/glider and driller/crawler identities remain distinct; no unreviewed interior-world entry or measured PA safety distance.

Heroes of Mandalore separates Tiber/Gar, surviving family, recording and current events; Thrawn’s form stays unresolved in the selected weapon-discussion still. Early draft motivations and the misleading Wren refusal wording are not new facts.

In the Name of the Rebellion separates Bail’s projection from the physical briefing, Saw’s remote/physical sequence, Edrio/Benthic/discarded Lorc, R4-C2’s real role/cut rivalry, Faos/Taos and current/old Titus ships. The cargo does not establish a present Death Star.

The Occupation separates reported Old Jho death, Rudor portrait/actual pursuit, Ryder transmission/actual rendezvous, Oleg alias and the hovering GAVr. Flight of the Defender separates elite prototype, salvaged components, actual probes/planned target use and blank trivia position 2.

Kindred preserves the unusual wolf journey without a spirit or later named-wolf claim. Rukh is Noghri, not the rejected Sith premise. Mothma’s form remains unspecified; physical Thrawn/Pryce bodies have selected released-image evidence; no exact final-base world, construction sphere or whole crashed Defender scene is inferred.

Secret Cargo has an actual E-XD-type infiltrator despite generic probe wording, a physical TIE defender, a Dantooine orbital meeting and unresolved individual forms for Pryce, Konstantine and Dodonna. Chandrila Mistress is sourced at series level without a forced episode hull.

Twin Suns distinguishes Kenobi’s recording/later body, Maul’s manipulation/physical duel, Kanan’s actual Atollon return/discarded Tatooine trip and Luke’s actual silhouette/reused Ezra model. Double Agent Droid separates Killun moon/station, baby neebrays and discarded Rishi concepts.

Zero Hour distinguishes Tarkin/Mon Mothma transmissions from physical officers, Kallus’s mixed remote/physical story and the named Krownest clan meeting. The blockade Interdictors are not Titus’s lost prototype. Phoenix Nest’s exact join to the captured carrier remains unresolved; no duplicate hull is invented. Yavin and Bendu’s prophecy remain future references.

Ghosts caption 7 misnames the surface companion as Rex; its image and captions 5/9 identify Zeb. Warhead has one blank narrative position. Production-scheduling trivia for Through Imperial Eyes does not replace its registered E17 identity. All discrepancies remain explicit.

Sato/Bail’s Ghost briefing and Hera’s training advice are remote. Kallus has remote warning plus a physical Warhead closing scene. Thrawn’s shipboard office is distinct from the Lothal factory room. Flash speeder is sourced at series level, while its Warhead scene, exact assassin-droid model and named shuttle/command hulls remain unresolved.

The Imperial Super Commandos gallery mislabels a destination Mandalore; the dedicated Protectors camp profile instead places its base on the third moon of the Concord Dawn system. Visions and Voices caption 7 misnames a possessed character; caption 9 and trivia 7 identify Kanan and Sabine. Both discrepancies remain explicit.

TIE defender plans do not establish a physical fighter appearance. Last Chance and Nightbrother need specifically identified episode hulls. Iron Squadron’s Sato participation is named, while his precise appearance form and named command hull remain unresolved. Maul’s early visions and later physical encounter are both described. Production numbers do not replace broadcast guide numbers.

Thrawn’s opener scenes are holographic transmissions; his Ryloth encounter is physical. Goran’s precise visible form and Hera’s final Agamar-related conversation remain unspecified. Original Phantom destruction and the recovered Phantom II stay separate, as do the RZ-1T trainer, generic A-wing and Sheathipede type/individual scopes.

Reklam’s salvaged Y-wings lack hyperdrives in that scene, without a universal Y-wing claim. Hobbie’s generic Biggs introduction conflicts with the released Wedge/Sabine-specific account; the discrepancy is explicit. Simulations, artwork, Legends origins and discarded outlines are not promoted to actual physical appearances.

Yoda’s remote Force contact, Anakin’s training recording plus vision, the Grand Inquisitor’s temple apparition and Vader’s separate physical arrival are explicitly distinguished. A combined guide never supplies unsourced per-part attribution.

Bahryn is a moon of Geonosis, the Lothal temple is distinct from Coruscant’s, and Malachor’s world and temple remain separate. Ketsu’s named participation has unspecified representation. Dicer has a sourced living scene before her disappearance; the finale’s closing Ahsoka image is retained without importing the later rescue.

Nixus Hub 218 has conflicting station/world descriptions across official trivia sources; this batch does not silently merge the current outpost with the existing station. Homecoming’s reinforcement is a light cruiser in the released narrative and Numa history but a Star Destroyer in Cham’s history; the discrepancy is visible and scoped.

Sato’s Homecoming appearance is a holographic transmission. Concord Dawn’s camp is on the third moon, separate from an unreviewed legacy planet. Lyste’s promotion retains one identity; Fang, Mining Guild fighters and the captured Quasar carrier do not inherit other hull or Legends specifications. Drawings, photos, memories and script-only labels are not promoted to living physical appearances.

Legacy parents are visions, Ryder and the tracked loth-cat have mixed vision/physical contexts, and Stealth Strike Kallus is a transmission. Blood Sisters names Bail at the rendezvous but the selected still does not establish physical versus holographic form; that row remains unspecified with a visible limitation.

The Blade Wing B6 prototype, GX1 starbus, Titus’s experimental Interdictor and Liberator remain distinct from production B-wings, old shuttles, generic/Legends models and the destroyed Phoenix Home. Chandel is a planned destination; Mustafar monitoring and decorative/design references do not establish visits.

Lando’s Siege hologram, the Emperor’s ending contact and Sato’s generator briefing are transmissions. Tua and Kallus retain direct rows when actual scenes accompany remote contact. Force sensing does not replace the actual physical scenes of Ahsoka, Kanan and Vader.

The modified Seelos walker, legacy AT-TE family, AT-AT family and distinct episode variant are scoped separately. The abandoned medical station shares a design with Kaliida Shoals but is not identified as that station. Nixus Hub 218, Tarkintown and the medical station are places, not additional planets. A single Ghost/Phantom caption inconsistency is explained, not copied into an unsupported ship location.

Trayvis’s vision, broadcast and physical meeting share one direct row with context. Alton/Trayvis interviews, Fulcrum’s remote conversation and Bail’s holographic greeting are transmissions. Ahsoka’s finale reveal and Vader’s Lothal arrival are direct scenes; later Kallus-Fulcrum biography is not assigned to the season-one contact.

The Sovereign, communications light-cruiser family, stolen rescue transport, Broken Horn and two distinct stolen/borrowed TIEs retain separate identities and scope. Mustafar is only a planned destination in Rebel Resolve but a system setting in the finale. No Gideon/Trask hull, generic Lambda, A-wing or technical metadata inferred.

Path of the Jedi distinguishes nightmare visions from direct scenes and Yoda’s remote communication through the Force. Mixed direct/vision contexts use one direct row with explanation; no real crew deaths or physical Yoda temple visit are asserted.

Fort Anaxes is the Rebels-era asteroid base. The displayed parade TIE and Inquisitor’s pursuit fighter are distinct. The Relentless has no assumed subclass and the landing shuttle has no assumed Lambda/Theta identity. No legacy technical fields inherited.

The combined Spark of Rebellion guide remains one review for parts 1–2. The later ABC Vader opening is excluded from original-pilot connections and remains a distinct documented version. No scene is assigned to an individual pilot part without evidence.

Obi-Wan’s holocron message, Trayvis’s broadcast and Luminara’s projected bait are transmissions. Luminara’s remains are also shown. Remote contacts followed by physical scenes use a single direct row with context; mentions, aliases and repeated names are not extra characters.
Episode inventory and writing credits do not establish every language mix, supplied master or frame-level version. Public references are not open media licences.

Normalized count: 75 numbered parts across four seasons (15/22/22/16), grouped into 66 official guide entries (14/20/19/13). This is an archive counting convention, not a universal count of playable streaming items. The four introductory shorts and the ABC revised pilot are excluded. Individual credits and appearances within combined parts are not inferred.

Current release-date research is restricted to the original US launch of each work and, when necessary to distinguish a documented version, its first US release. Existing sourced events are retained. Worldwide/Finland dates, later platform availability, routine rereleases and exhaustive master comparisons are deferred rather than factually resolved.

notes: All 33 narrative captions and five trivia captions read, including both Show More expansions. One combined official guide covers numbered parts 15–16; no unsupported split of links between parts or new release dates.

The main Lothal battle and the later post-Endor epilogue are distinct time contexts. Jacen physically appears with Hera/Chopper in the epilogue. Endor is narrated, while the selected still shows a cockpit; no Endor setting row is inferred. Lira San is the explicitly described later Zeb/Kallus trip, not the main battle setting.

Palpatine is explicitly a holo-projection. Its crackling reveals another appearance, not a new physical body on the Chimaera. Ezra’s parents occur in an earlier stored holo and in a tempting doorway depiction; one unspecified row per parent preserves these mixed forms without certifying resurrection or their physical return.

Ezra is physically present during the main confrontation and later heard in a recorded farewell. His direct row explicitly notes the recording as a second form, not a second live Ezra aboard the Ghost after his departure. Ahsoka’s physical epilogue appearance does not retrospectively place her at the main battle.

The named Chimaera is established by the transported Temple section in trivia 2 and the selected official Ezra history. It is distinct from the generic Star Destroyer type and every earlier unnamed blockade hull. A portal fragment aboard ship is not proof of a new whole original-Temple location visit or a realm entry.

Gregor’s fatal injury, Melch’s survival, Rukh’s death in the activated generator and Pryce’s death with the exploding base are explicitly distinguished. No exact death date or unverified surname is added.

Purrgil physically arrive and carry the ship away; Sabine’s painted shoulder motif is art, not another live animal. The destination is unknown within this guide: no current Peridea setting, death, exact hyperspace coordinates or instant reference to later Ahsoka events.

Crimson guards in released still 17 match the named Emperor-protecting force. No individual guard names, biological species, universal height or weapon subtype is inferred. Generator design reuse from Endor is not the same location or a new Return of the Jedi scene.
